title: The Library Parade and the Cart with Three Jobs
premise: In a little library town, Mayor Mallow boasts that her parade must be the biggest ever. Nia, the child librarian, and Tuck, a cheerful cart builder, discover that one shared cart can become a grand parade float, a rolling bookmobile, or a tiny traveling reading room—depending on what they believe, want, and choose.
cast_and_props: Characters: mayor Mallow (wants the biggest parade and enjoys being admired), Nia (wants books to reach children who cannot visit the library), and Tuck (wants his beautifully balanced cart to be useful and appreciated). Shared setting: the library square and parade lane. Props: one wooden cart, a banner, a stack of library books, and a brass bell. Keep all state keys attached to these entities: mayor.memes.Boast, nia.memes.Care, tuck.memes.Craft, cart.owner, cart.location, cart.decorated, cart.loaded, cart.mode, cart.performer, banner.attached, bell.rung, and knowledge slots such as nia.knows.cart.loaded.
kernels_and_interactions: Use five kernel families: (1) motives and meme changes; (2) observe/tell for mistaken beliefs; (3) transfer for cart or banner ownership; (4) loading, decorating, and locating concrete props; (5) performance and social agreement. An observation must enable a later choice: Nia can observe that the book stack is waiting for delivery, while Mallow can observe that the cart is empty. Tuck can tell Mallow that the cart's hidden folding shelves exist only after he has learned she wants a giant float. Shared scenes should include Nia's invitation to the square, Tuck showing the cart's folding shelves, a group cart move, and the final bell ring.
seed_parameters: Seed 955885281. Declare initial premise keys such as cart.owner, cart.location, cart.loaded, mayor.want, and tuck.knows.cart.shelves. Vary three physical/social starts: A: the cart belongs to Mallow, is empty, and she has invited everyone to make a giant float; B: the cart belongs to Tuck, is already loaded with books, and he has promised Nia a delivery; C: the cart belongs to Nia, is parked at the library door, and Mallow mistakenly believes the book stack is a parade audience. Outcomes should be concrete: cart.mode in ('float','bookmobile','reading_room'), cart.location at the parade lane or neighborhood stop, and cart.owner or cart.performer reflecting the final arrangement.
candidate_scenes: Use 16 candidates, with 5–10 selected. Opening/bridge IDs: invite_square, look_cart, look_books, tell_cart_purpose, tell_folding_shelves. Choices and consequences: claim_cart_for_parade (Mallow takes ownership only when allowed), transfer_cart_to_nia, load_books, unload_books, attach_banner, fold_shelves, move_cart_to_square, move_cart_to_neighborhood, ring_bell, invite_children, perform_big_loop, perform_book_route, perform_reading_room. Reuse look_cart, tell_folding_shelves, attach_banner, move_cart_to_square, and ring_bell across paths. Make three pivotal scenes only: tell_cart_purpose (Mallow's boast changes toward usefulness), fold_shelves (Tuck chooses to reveal the cart's secret), and invite_children (Nia changes from guarding the books to sharing them). The inciting action must be invite_square or an observed book-delivery promise, before anyone responds.
constraints: Do not use counters or branch numbers. Every slot is declared before use, and every candidate has real preconditions. The three problems are: Mallow treats an empty cart as a contest float; Tuck's promised book delivery conflicts with the parade; and Mallow mistakes waiting library children or stacked books for parade spectators. Their endings must differ: a towering decorated float rolls past admiring crowds; a bell-led bookmobile delivers books to neighborhood children; or the cart opens into a cozy reading room where the parade pauses to listen. No character may speak knowledge gained only later. Use 2–4 characters, scalar state only, prune=True, 12–22 candidates, and premise_keys/outcome_keys naming actual declared properties.
different_endings: Ending 1: After perform_big_loop, the banner is high, the cart.mode is float, and Mallow rides proudly while Tuck rings the bell; the last image is the cart casting a giant shadow shaped like a crown. Ending 2: After perform_book_route, cart.mode is bookmobile and cart.location is neighborhood_stop; children choose books as the brass bell gives a friendly ding, and Mallow's enormous banner becomes a roof of shade. Ending 3: After perform_reading_room, cart.mode is reading_room and invite_children is complete; the parade gathers around the unfolded shelves, and the cart's wheels disappear beneath a soft circle of listening feet. Provide at least two conditional prose variants for each ending and two opening variants, with phrase slots for variable modes and locations.
